_: Codex's rung of the lane ladder. Paired name-for-name with .agents/lanes/claude.json: the same LN means the same *relative* capability on both harnesses, so a skill declares `lane: L4` once and each harness resolves it to its own model. These two files are the only two places in the repo a model name may appear. Rungs are ordered L1 (most capable) to L7 (cheapest).
$comment_skill_supports_effort: Whether this harness accepts an effort key in SKILL.md front matter. Codex does not, so a Codex skill payload gets the rung's model alone and the rung's effort reaches it only through a lane agent.

L1.summary: Plans and design decisions of any size, where the work decides how something should be built.
L1.why: frontier family at the setting above `high`. Planning and design: authoring a plan, large or small, that takes a design position; architecture; a data model or contract; a mechanism choice. The agent picks it on its own judgement. Never implementation, review or delivery; a merge, push or publish at the end of a job never raises its lane.

L2.summary: High-stakes judgement that is not design, where a wrong call is costly or hard to undo.
L2.why: top general family at the setting above `high`. Judgement with a lot riding on it that designs nothing: a diagnosis of a production failure, a security or migration review. Delivering a change never selects it; merge, push and publish are governed by the delivery gates.

L3.summary: Open-ended judgement that is not design, where the answer is not yet known.
L3.why: top general family at its default setting. Open-ended judgement that designs nothing: a diagnosis with no known answer, an investigation, weighing evidence a test cannot settle.

L4.summary: Ordinary specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch, delivery included.
L4.why: the general family at reduced effort. Specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch: features, bugfixes, review lenses, and the review, CI and merge that deliver them.

L5.summary: Mechanical work whose shape is already decided.
L5.why: the small family at high effort. Mechanical work whose shape is already decided: scripted edits, docs, ledger upkeep.

L6.summary: Bulk clerical work whose input is too large for the cheapest rung.
L6.why: the small family at medium effort. Clerical loops and bulk passes -- a monitor, a long transcript, a big diff -- that outgrow the floor rung.

L7.summary: Clerical work with a small input and no judgement to make.
L7.why: the small family at low effort. Clerical work with a small input: commit, push, pull, sync, one poll.

frontier.summary: Frontier deliberation above the ladder, priced by provenance rather than by task shape.
frontier.why: valid only when the user explicitly asks for this tier or its model by name. Deliberately not a rung: the four lane questions grade task shape, and no answer to them may select this spend. L1 prices the same family one effort step below, and a test asserts no rung prices this exact model-and-effort pair, so lane inflation can never reach it.

$comment_context_ceiling: null means unrecorded, not unlimited. The Claude table carries real per-model windows from the published model table; the Codex figures are not verified here, so recording a number would be inventing one. A lane consumer that needs a ceiling must treat null as 'unknown' and not assume the input fits.
